coverage.evidence: The eight keys charity.name, link, raised, target, percent and bar (CharityCampaignHelpers.cs:18-43) and charity.donations.count and latest (CharityDonationHelpers.cs:138-146) render only when args.Count is 0 (LiveCharityRows.cs:90-121), which matches 'None of these helpers takes an input'.

Money keeps Twitch's decimal places with culture grouping, puts the symbol first and the code after the amount when the symbol is unknown (LiveText.cs:60-67). Percent is null when the target is <= 0, rounded away from zero and not clamped (LiveText.cs:36-37). Bar is 10 blocks of full/pale, clamped to 0..100 and rounded, then the percent (LiveText.cs:40-50; MeterBars.cs:25,30). Link is null when the website is blank (CharityCampaignHelpers.cs:19-23). Culture is Channel.Language, en-US when unset (TemplateRenderScope.cs:37; NumberCulture.cs:22-35; ChannelService.cs:593).

Rows use TemplateHelperContexts.Standard (LiveEventRow.cs:168-175), which is every context except Viewer (TemplateHelperContexts.cs:21-22). That matches command, event response, timer, pipeline, Discord and webhook, and not viewer text, even with Viewer Templates on (FeatureService.cs:92-93).

LiveCharityData makes one Lazy fetch of the Twitch charity campaign per render (LiveCharityData.cs:73-93), and the campaign is null on failure or on an empty response (LiveCharityData.cs:101-107; TwitchHelixTransport.cs:107-110). Nothing is cached in the transport, so each reply asks Twitch again.

One page of donations at the default page size of 100 (LiveCharityData.cs:109-116; TwitchPage.cs:15). Total defaults to 0 (TwitchHelixTransport.cs:139), so count = Math.Max(Total, Items.Count) is capped at 100 and gives 0 for an empty list (CharityDonationHelpers.cs:138). Latest is null with no items and otherwise reads 'UserName (Money)' (CharityDonationHelpers.cs:143-146).

A null render prints the token as typed and the rest of the reply still renders (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:19,44). The scope pre-check for channel:read:charity makes both calls fail without the permission (TwitchCharityApi.cs:32-55,57-89; TwitchTokenResolver.cs:237-266,319-357). The gap is recorded (MissingScopeRecordingHandler.cs:42-99) and shown as the Needs attention item with Dismiss (TwitchGrantGapSource.cs:75,107-149; locales en.json:1130-1132). The grant flow matches MissingTwitchScopesNotice.vue:28,51-85, twitchHealth.ts:172-179, settings/integrations en.json:7-11, locales en.json:48-52, ActionDefinitionSeeder.cs:305 and AuthService.cs:219.

reader_answers.evidence: The eight helper names and the no-argument rule match CharityCampaignHelpers.cs:18-43, CharityDonationHelpers.cs:138-146 and LiveCharityRows.cs:90-121.

channel:read:charity is pre-checked (TwitchCharityApi.cs:32-55) and is not in the base broadcaster sign-in (TwitchLoginScopes.cs:54-61). Grant permissions on Integrations is shown to twitch:diagnostics:read, which is Moderator (MissingTwitchScopesNotice.vue:28,76-85; ActionDefinitionSeeder.cs:305). The permission is saved on the Twitch account that approves (AuthService.cs:219).

The approved title is shown after approval (MissingTwitchScopesNotice.vue:51-53; locales en.json:48-52). Braces print on null (TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:19,44). The three causes map to the scope pre-check (TwitchCharityApi.cs:32-55), no campaign (TwitchHelixTransport.cs:107-110) and a failed call (LiveCharityData.cs:101-107).

The reply and the empty-donation fallback match CharityDonationHelpers.cs:143-146, and every helper in that reply is null with no campaign (LiveCharityData.cs:101-116). The reader's wider claim that every charity helper prints as typed with no campaign goes beyond the page, which says 'every helper in the reply' at charity.mdx:120. The source does not support that claim for {charity.donations.count}: donations are read without a campaign check and give 0 on an empty successful page (LiveCharityData.cs:109-116; CharityDonationHelpers.cs:138).
